skill.name: explore
skill.tagline: Ask, sort, research, experiment — the model drives, the user rules.
skill.shortSummary: A design-discussion skill that turns open questions into evidence-backed decisions using Ask, Sort, Research, and Experiment moves.
skill.fullSummary: Explore drives design discussions through four moves: Ask, Sort, Research, and Experiment. Ask raises purpose, alternative, and shortcut questions at the model first, then brings the user only well-shaped user-bound questions; Sort classifies every open question as world fact, user-held fact, or judgment; Research settles world facts through the cheapest sufficient source; Experiment creates evidence when nothing existing holds the answer. The model drives; each pass ends with labeled findings.

highlights.title: Four Disciplined Moves
highlights.description: Ask, Sort, Research, and Experiment structure every design question. Questions are sorted as world fact, user-held fact, or judgment before any work proceeds, and unsorted questions never reach the user.

highlights.title: Model Drives, User Rules
highlights.description: The model raises the hard questions itself and answers everything its own instruments can reach, leaving the user only their own facts and rulings — never legwork.

highlights.title: Cheapest Sufficient Evidence
highlights.description: Research follows a source order of memory, this machine, then the web. Load-bearing recalled facts are verified against their sources before a recommendation rests on them.

highlights.title: Transparent Rulings
highlights.description: Every pass presents purpose, explored alternatives, the strongest shortcut, and the recommendation, with facts, judgments, assumptions, and parked items each labeled as what they are.

steps.name: Ask
steps.description: Raise purpose, alternatives, and shortcut questions, then bring user-bound questions.
steps.details: Raise purpose, alternatives, and shortcut questions at the model first; keep the best-guess summary and open question list visible; ask one call of up to four well-shaped user-bound questions.

steps.name: Sort
steps.description: Classify every open question before any work proceeds.
steps.details: Mark each question as world fact, user-held fact, or judgment; mark user-bound questions; route third-party or access-gated facts as routing requests; prepare ambiguous questions as judgments.

steps.name: Research
steps.description: Settle world facts through the cheapest sufficient source.
steps.details: Follow memory, this machine, then the web, escalating only when a source cannot settle. Verify load-bearing recalls, run one scouting pass per settled intent, and compile a digest naming gaps.

steps.name: Experiment
steps.description: Create evidence when nothing existing holds the answer.
steps.details: Run probes against real artifacts, record commands and outputs beside briefs, and get go-ahead for trials that spend money or touch external systems. Invoke /attune:experiment for blind comparisons.

steps.name: Present
steps.description: Present the pass's findings with all items labeled.
steps.details: State current purpose, explored alternatives, strongest shortcut, recommendation with rationale, and unverified or parked items. Label facts, evidence, judgments, and recommendations as such.
